subject: Food Science
title: World War II Military Rations
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: World War II Military Rations.

hook.text: World War II Military Rations: a surprising example shows why better reasoning matters.

buildup.text: The K-ration provided 3,000 calories per day in a pocket-sized package: crackers, canned meat, candy bars, and instant coffee.

discovery.text: Spray-dried eggs, dehydrated vegetables, and instant coffee were perfected for military use.

twist.text: M&M's were invented in 1941 for soldiers—the candy shell prevented chocolate from melting in tropical climates.

climax.text: Post-war food technology flooded civilian markets: frozen dinners (1953), Tang (1957), freeze-dried foods, and microwave ovens.

punchline.text: War demanded portable, durable food. Peace got frozen dinners, M&M's, and instant coffee.

quiz.question: Why were M&M's originally invented?
options: For soldiers—the candy shell prevented chocolate from melting in tropical climates
